transcription.tex: Question 14

A rough plane surface is inclined at an angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\sin \alpha=\frac{5}{13}\). A packet of mass 8 kg is pulled at a constant speed up a line of greatest slope of the plane. The coefficient of friction between the packet and the plane is 0.3.\par Problem-solving\par Draw a right-angled triangle with sides of length 5, 12 and 13, or use your calculator to find the exact value of \(\cos \alpha.\)\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the packet. [5 marks]\par The packet moves a distance of 15 m up the plane. Calculate:\par \textbf{b)} the work done against friction [3 marks]\par \textbf{c)} the work done against gravity. [4 marks]

\(\mu = 0.3\)\par a Resolving perpendicular to the plane:\par \(R = 8g \cos \alpha\) [M1]\par \(= 8g \times \frac{12}{13}\) [A1]\par Friction is limiting:\par \(F = \mu R\) [M1]\par \(F = 0.3 \times 8 \times 9.8 \times \frac{12}{13}\) [A1]\par \(= 21.71\ldots\)\par The frictional force has magnitude \(21.7 \text{ N}\) (3 s.f.). [A1]
b Work done against friction \(= Fs\) [M1]\par \(= 21.71\ldots \times 15\) [A1]\par \(= 325.6\ldots\)

The work done against friction is \(326 \text{ J}\) (3 s.f.). [A1]\par c Work done against gravity \(= mgh\) [M1]\par \(= 8 \times 9.8 \times (15 \sin \alpha)\) [M1]\par \(= 8 \times 9.8 \times \left(15 \times \frac{5}{13}\right)\) [A1]\par \(= 452.3\ldots\)\par The work done against gravity is \(452 \text{ J}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 15

A rough surface is inclined at an angle \(\arcsin{\frac{7}{25}}\) to the horizontal. A particle of mass 0.5kg is pulled 3m at a constant speed up the surface by a force acting along a line of greatest slope. The only resistances to the motion are those due to friction and gravity. The work done by the force is 12 J. Calculate the coefficient of friction between the particle and the surface. [5 marks]

Resolving perpendicular to the plane:\par \(R = 0.5g \cos \theta\) [B1]\par \(= 0.5g \times \frac{24}{25}\)\par Resolving parallel to the plane:\par \(T = F + 0.5g \sin \theta\) [M1]\par Friction is limiting:\par \(F = \mu R\) [M1]\par \(F = \mu \times 0.5g \times \frac{24}{25}\)\par \(T = \mu \times 0.5g \times \frac{24}{25} + 0.5g \times \frac{7}{25}\)
Work done by force \(= \text{force} \times \text{distance moved}\)\par \(12 = T \times 3\) [M1]

\(T = 4\)\par \(\therefore 4 = \mu \times 0.5g \times \frac{24}{25} + 0.5g \times \frac{7}{25}\)\par \(\mu = \frac{4 - 0.5 \times 9.8 \times \frac{7}{25}}{0.5 \times 9.8 \times \frac{24}{25}}\)\par \(\mu = 0.5586\dots\)\par The coefficient of friction is 0.559 (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 16

A rough surface is inclined at \(40^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. A box of mass 1.5kg is pulled at a constant speed up the surface by a force T acting along a line of greatest slope. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the surface is 0.4. Modelling the box as a particle, calculate the work done by T when the particle travels 8m. [4 marks]

\(\mu=0.4\)\par Resolving perpendicular to the plane:\par \(R=1.5 g \cos 40^{\circ}\)\par Friction is limiting:\par \(F=\mu R\)\par \(F=0.4 \times 1.5 g \cos 40^{\circ}\) [M1]\par Resolving parallel to the plane:\par \(T=F+1.5 g \sin 40^{\circ}\) [M1]\par \(T=0.4 \times 1.5 g \cos 40^{\circ}+1.5 g \sin 40^{\circ}\)\par Work done by \(T=T \times s\)
\(=(0.4 \times 1.5 g \cos 40^{\circ}+1.5 g \sin 40^{\circ}) \times 8\) [M1]\par \(=111.6 \dots\)
The work done by \(T\) is 112 J (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 17

A particle P of mass 2kg is projected up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane which is inclined at an angle \(\arcsin\frac{3}{5}\) to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between P and the plane is 0.35.\par The particle comes to instantaneous rest a distance 3m up the line of greatest slope of the plane. Find:\par \textbf{a)} the work done by gravity [3 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the work done by friction [3 marks]\par \textbf{c)} the speed of projection. [4 marks]

\(\sin \alpha=\frac{3}{5}\Rightarrow\cos \alpha=\frac{4}{5}\)\par Work done = force distance moved in direction of force\par \textbf{a)} Gravity acts downwards while the particle gains height, so its work is \(W_g=-mgh\). [M1]\par Weight, \(W=mg=2g\), \(h=3\sin\alpha=\frac{9}{5}\) m [A1]\par \(W_g=-2g\times 9/5\).\par \(W_g=-2\times9.8\times1.8=-35.28\;\mathrm J\).

Gravity does −35.3 J of work (3 s.f.). The gravitational potential energy increases by 35.3 J. [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Friction opposes the displacement, so \(W_F=-Fs\), where \(s=3\;\mathrm m\).\par Normal reaction force, \(R\), can be found by resolving perpendicular to the slope:
\(R=2g\cos\alpha\) [M1]\par \(R=\frac{8}{5}g\)

So frictional force, \(F=\frac{7}{20}\times\frac{8}{5}g=\frac{14}{25}g\) [M1]\par \(W_F=-\frac{14}{25}g\times 3\).\par \(W_F=-0.56\times9.8\times3=-16.464\;\mathrm J\).\par Friction does −16.5 J of work (3 s.f.). [A1]\par \textbf{c)} Work done against these forces = kinetic energy lost kinetic energy \(=\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\) so here: [M1]\par \(35.28+16.464=\left(\frac{1}{2}\times 2u^{2}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 0^{2}\right)\) [M1] [A1]\par \(51.744=u^{2}\)\par \(u=7.1933\ldots\), so the speed of projection is \(7.19\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) (3 s.f.). [A1]

transcription.tex: A small package P is modelled as a particle of mass 0.6 kg. The package slides down a rough plane from a point S to a point T, where \(ST=12 \mathrm{m}\). The plane is inclined at an angle of \(30^{\circ}\) to the horizontal and \(ST\) is a line of greatest slope of the plane, as shown in Figure 3. The speed of P at S is \(10 \mathrm{m} \mathrm{s}^{-1}\) and the speed of P at T is \(9 \mathrm{m} \mathrm{s}^{-1}\).\par (a) Calculate the total loss of energy of P in moving from S to T,\par [4 marks]\par (b) Given that the work done against friction by P is equal to total loss of energy of P in moving from S to T, calculate the coefficient of friction between P and the plane.\par [5 marks]

(a) KE lost is \(\frac{1} {2} \times 0.6 \times\left( 10^{2}-9^{2} \right) \left(= 5.7 \mathrm{~J}\right)\)\par PE lost is \(0.6 \times 9.8 \times 12 \sin 30^{\circ} \left(= 35.28 \mathrm{~J}\right)\)\par Total loss in energy is 41.0 (J)\par (b) \(R=0.6 \times 9.8 \times\cos 30^{\circ} \left( \approx 5.09 \right)\)\par WE \(40.98=\mu \times 0.6 \times 9.8 \times\cos 30^{\circ} \times 12\)\par \(\mu\approx0.67\) or 0.671
Question 7

A playground slide is modelled as a plane inclined at \(48^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. A child of mass 25 kg slides down the slide for 4 m.\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the potential energy lost by the child. [4 marks]\par \textbf{b)} State one assumption that you have made in your calculations, and comment on its validity. [1 mark]

P.E. lost \(= mgh\) [M1]\par \(= 25 \times 9.8 \times(4 \sin 48^{\circ})\) [M1]\par \(= 728.2 \dots\) [A1]\par The P.E. lost by the child is 728 J (3 s.f.) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Model the child as a particle whose centre of mass descends through the same vertical distance as the slide.\par This is reasonable if the child stays in the same posture. The gravitational potential energy lost depends only on the vertical fall. [B1]
Question 8

A ball of mass 0.6kg is dropped from a height of 2m into a pond.\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the kinetic energy of the ball as it hits the surface of the water. [3 marks]\par The ball begins to sink in the water with a speed of \(4.8 \mathrm{~ m s}^{-1}\).\par \textbf{b)} Calculate the kinetic energy lost when the ball strikes the water. [4 marks]

\textbf{a)} \(s=2 \mathrm{~m}, a=9.8 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{s}^{-2}, u=0, v=?\)\par \(v^{2}=u^{2}+2 a s\) [M1]\par \(v^{2}=0+2 \times 9.8 \times 2\)\par \(v^{2}=39.2\)\par K.E. \(=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times 39.2\) [M1]\par \(=11.76\)\par The K.E. of the ball as it hits the surface of the water is 11.8 J (3 s.f.) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} K.E. lost \(=\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\) [M1]\par \(=11.76-\frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times 4.8^{2}\) [M1] [A1]\par \(=4.848\)\par The K.E. lost by the ball is 4.85 J (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 10

A car of mass 750kg moves along a stretch of road which can be modelled as a line of greatest slope of a plane inclined to the horizontal at \(30^{\circ}\). As the car moves up the road for 500m its speed reduces from \(20 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) to \(15 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\). Calculate:\par \textbf{a)} the loss of kinetic energy of the car [3 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the gain of potential energy of the car. [4 marks]

\(\mathrm{K.E.}=\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\) [M1]\par \(=\frac{1}{2}\times 750 \times 20^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\times 750 \times 15^{2}\) [A1]\par \(=65625\)\par The loss of K.E of the car is 65 625 J [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Gain of P.E.=mgh [M1]\par \(=750 \times 9.8 \times(500 \sin 30^{\circ})\) [M1] [A1]\par \(=1837500\)\par The gain of P.E. of the car is 1 837 500 J [A1]
Question 11
A woman of mass 80kg climbs a vertical cliff face of height h m. Her potential energy increases by 15.7kJ.\par Find the height of the cliff. [3 marks]
P.E. = mgh [M1]\par \(15.7 \times1000=80 \times9.8 h\) [A1]\par \(h=\frac{15.7 \times1000}{80 \times9.8}\)\par \(h=20.02\)\par The cliff is 20.0 m high (3 s.f.) [A1]

parts.text: Work in + Initial K.E. + Initial G.P.E. = Final K.E. + Final G.P.E. + Work out
The law of Conservation of Energy: the total energy of an isolated system remains constant
Some of the initial energy might have been stored in an engine or battery that then does work, transferring this energy to another form.
Some of the energy may be ‘lost’ if the object did work against a resistive force which transfers some energy into heat (and perhaps sound etc.)

transcription.tex: [Textbook] A skier is moving downhill and passes point A on a ski run at \(6\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). After descending 50m vertically the run begins to ascend. When the skier has ascended 25m to the point B her speed is \(4\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The skier and her skis have a combined mass of 55kg. The total distance she travels from A to B is 1400m. The non-gravitational resistances to motion are constant and have a total magnitude of 12N. Calculate the work done by the skier.

shapes.alt: Cross-country skier pushing uphill with poles

transcription.tex: Use energy at A + work done by the skier = energy at B + work against resistance. Take the lowest point as zero gravitational potential energy.\par \(W+\tfrac12(55)(6^2)+55(9.8)(50)=\tfrac12(55)(4^2)+55(9.8)(25)+12(1400)\).\par \(W=2780\;\mathrm J\) (3 s.f.).
Tip: Gravity supplies energy on the descent. The skier can also do work by pushing with the poles, as shown in the second photograph.

transcription.tex: Question 5

A box of mass 3kg is projected from point A across a rough horizontal floor with speed \(6 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{s}^{-1}\) The box moves in a straight line across the floor and comes to rest at point B.The coefficient of friction between the box and the floor is 0.4.\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the kinetic energy lost by the box. [2 marks]\par \textbf{b)} Write down the work done against friction. [1 mark]\par \textbf{c)} Calculate the distance AB. [5 marks]

\(\mu=0.4\)\par \textbf{a)} K.E. lost \(=\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\) [M1]\par \(=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 6^{2}-0\)\par \(=54\)\par The kinetic energy lost by the box is 54 J [A1]\par \textbf{b)} The work done against friction is 54 J [B1]

\textbf{c)} Resolving perpendicular to the floor: \(R=3 g\) [M1] Friction is limiting: \(F=\mu R\) [M1]\par \(F=0.4 \times3 g\) [M1] Work done \(= F s\)\par \(54=0.4 \times3 g \times s\) [A1]\par \(s=\frac{54}{0.4 \times3 g}=4.591 \dots\) [A1] The distance AB is 4.59 m (3 s.f.)
Question 10

A bullet of mass 150g travelling at \(500 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) horizontally hits a vertical wall. The resistive force exerted by the wall on the bullet is modelled as having a constant magnitude of 250000N.\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the distance that the bullet penetrates the wall. [4 marks]\par \textbf{b)} State how the model for the resistive force could be refined to make it more realistic. [1 mark]

10a Loss of K.E \(= \frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\) [M1]\par \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 0.15 \times 500^{2}-0\) Work done by resistance \(= F s\) [M1]\par \(= 250000 s\) Work done by resistance \(= \mathrm{loss}\) of K.E. \(250000 s=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.15 \times 500^{2}\) [A1]\par \(s=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times 0.15 \times 500^{2}}{250000}\)\par \(= 0.075\) [A1] The distance the bullet penetrates the wall is 0.075 m (or 75 mm)\par \textbf{b)} The resistive force could depend on the speed of the bullet. [B1]
Question 15

A box of mass 2kg is projected with speed \(6 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{s}^{-1}\) up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at \(30^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the box and the plane is \(\frac{1}{3}\). Use the work-energy principle to calculate the distance the box travels up the plane before coming to rest. [5 marks]

K.E. lost \(= \frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\)\par \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 6^{2}-0\)\par \(= 36\) [B1]\par P.E. gained \(= m g h\)\par \(= 2 \times 9.8 \times( x \sin 30^{\circ})\)\par \(= 9.8 x\) [M1]\par Resolving perpendicular to the plane: \(R=2 g \cos 30^{\circ}\)\par Friction is limiting: \(F=\mu R\)
\(F=\frac{1}{3} \times 2 g \cos 30^{\circ}=\frac{2}{3} g \cos 30^{\circ}\) [M1]\par Work done against friction \(F x=\frac{2}{3} g x \cos 30^{\circ}\)
K.E. lost \(= P.E.\) gained \(+\) work done against friction

\(\Rightarrow 36=9.8 x+\frac{2}{3} g x \cos 30^{\circ}\) [M1]\par \(36=9.8 x \left( 1+\frac{2}{3} \cos 30^{\circ} \right)\)\par \(x=\frac{36}{9.8 \left( 1+\frac{2}{3} \cos 30^{\circ} \right)}=2.328 \dots\)\par The particle moves 2.33 m up the plane (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 16

A tennis ball of mass 58 g is hit vertically upwards by a tennis racket from a point 1 metre above the ground. Given that the tennis ball receives an impulse of 1.7 Ns,\par \textbf{a)} find the initial speed of the ball. [3 marks]\par The ball first comes to rest at a point 28 m above the ground.\par \textbf{b)} Find the energy lost due to air resistance by the ball during this motion. [3 marks]\par Given that the air resistance is modelled as a constant force of magnitude RN,\par \textbf{c)} find the value of R. [2 marks]

\textbf{a)} Resolving vertically:\par \(I=mv-mu\) [M1]\par \(1.7=0.058 v-0.058 \times 0\) [A1]\par \(v=\frac{1.7}{0.058}\)\par \(v=29.31 \dots\)\par The initial speed of the ball is \(29.3 \mathrm{~ m} \mathrm{s}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Energy lost = initial kinetic energy - final potential energy\par \(=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}-m g h\) [M1]
The energy lost due to air resistance is \(9.57 \mathrm{~ J}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]

\textbf{c)} Work done against air resistance = energy lost\par \(R \times 27=9.566 \dots\) [M1]\par \(R=\frac{9.566 \dots}{27}\)\par \(R=0.354 \dots\)\par The value of \(R\) is \(0.354\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 17

A skier of mass 80kg skis down a straight hill inclined at \(30^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The speed of the skier increases from \(3 \mathrm{~m s}^{-1}\) to \(12 \mathrm{~m s}^{-1}\).\par The total resistances to motion of the skier due to friction and air resistance are modelled as a constant force of magnitude RN.\par \textbf{a)} Given that the skier travels a total distance of 50m, find the value of R. [5 marks]\par \textbf{b)} Suggest one way in which the model could be refined. [1 mark]

\textbf{a)} Work done by resistive forces on the skier \(=\) change in total energy of the skier Loss in P.E. \(= mgh\)\par Increase in K.E. \(= \frac{1}{2} m v^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}\) [M1]\par Total loss of energy \(=\) P.E. lost \(-\) K.E. gained\par \(= mgh+\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\) [M1]\par Force \(\times\) distance \(= mgh+\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}\) [M1]
\(50 R \equiv( 80 \times9.8 \times50 \sin 30^{\circ})+\left( \frac{1}{2} \times80 \times3^{2} \right)-\left( \frac{1}{2} \times80 \times12^{2} \right)\) [A1]

\(50 R=14\ 200\)\par \(R=284\)\par The magnitude of the resistive force is \(284\;\mathrm{N}\). [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Allow the resistive force to depend on speed, for example by modelling air resistance separately from friction at the skis. [B1]
Question 18

A box of mass 70 kg starts at rest and slides in a straight line down a surface inclined at \(20^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. After the box has travelled a distance of 60 m, the surface becomes horizontal, and the box slides a further 50 m before coming to rest. The total resistance due to friction and air resistance is modelled as a force of constant magnitude RN which acts so as to oppose the direction of motion of the box. Find the value of R. [7 marks]

Change in K.E. \(= \frac{1}{2} m v^2 - \frac{1}{2} m u^2\)\par \(= 0 - 0\) [B1]\par Loss of P.E. \(= m g h\) [M1]\par \(= 70 \times 9.8 \times (60 \sin 20^\circ)\) [A1]\par Work done against resistance \(= F s\)\par \(= R \times (60 + 50)\) [M1]\par \(= 110 R\)\par Work done against resistance \(= \text{loss of P.E.}\) [M1]\par \(110 R = 70 \times 9.8 \times (60 \sin 20^\circ)\) [A1]
\(R = \frac{70 \times 9.8 \times 60 \sin 20^\circ}{\dots 110}\)\par \(R = 127.9\)
The value of \(R\) is 128 (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 19

A girl and her sledge have a combined mass of 40kg. She starts from rest and descends a slope which is inclined at \(25^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. At the bottom of the slope the ground becomes horizontal for 15m before rising at \(6^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The girl travels 25m up the slope before coming to rest once more. There is a constant resistance to motion of magnitude 18N. Calculate the distance the girl travels down the slope initially. [7 marks]

Loss of P.E. \(= mgh\)\par \(= 40 \times 9.8 \times (x \sin 25^{\circ} - 25 \sin 6^{\circ})\) [M1] [A1]\par Change in K.E. \(= \frac{1}{2} m v^{2} - \frac{1}{2} m u^{2}\)\par \(= 0 - 0\) [B1]\par Work done against resistance \(= Fs\)\par \(= 18 \times (x + 15 + 25)\) [M1]\par \(= 18 \times (x + 40)\)\par Work done against resistance \(= \text{loss of P.E.}\) [M1]
\(18x + 18 \times 40 = 40 \times 9.8 \times x \sin 25^{\circ} - 40 \times 9.8 \times 25 \sin 6^{\circ}\)
\((40 \times 9.8 \sin 25^{\circ} - 18)x = 18 \times 40 + 40 \times 9.8 \times 25 \sin 6^{\circ}\) [M1]
\(x = \frac{18 \times 40 + 40 \times 9.8 \times 25 \sin 6^{\circ}}{40 \times 9.8 \sin 25^{\circ} - 18}\)\par \(x = 11.81\ldots\)\par The girl travels \(11.8 \text{ m}\) down the slope. [A1]

transcription.tex: A girl and her bicycle have a combined mass of 64 kg. She cycles up a straight stretch of road which is inclined at an angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\sin \alpha=\frac{1}{14}\). She cycles at a constant speed of 5 m s \(^{-1}\). When she is cycling at this speed, the resistance to motion from non-gravitational forces has magnitude 20 N.\par (a) Find the rate at which the cyclist is working. [4 marks]
(a) Resolving uphill: \(F=20+64g\sin\alpha\)  M1\par \(=64.8\,\mathrm{N}\)  A1\par \(P=Fv=64.8\times5=324\,\mathrm W\)  M1 A1 [4 marks]
Question 7

A car of mass 850kg is travelling along a straight horizontal road against resistances totalling 350N. The car's engine is working at 9kW. Calculate:\par \textbf{a)} the acceleration when the car is travelling at \(7 \mathrm{~m s}^{-1}\) [3 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the acceleration when the car is travelling at \(15 \mathrm{~m s}^{-1}\) [2 marks]\par \textbf{c)} the maximum speed of the car. [2 marks]

Power \(= Fv\)\par \(9000 = T \times 7\) [M1]\par \(T = \frac{9000}{7}\)\par Now using \(F = ma\):\par \(T - 350 = ma\)\par \(\frac{9000}{7} - 350 = 850a\) [M1]\par \(a = \frac{\frac{9000}{7} - 350}{850}\)\par \(a = 1.100\ldots\)\par The acceleration is \(1.10 \text{ m s}^{-2}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]\par b\par Power \(= Fv\)
\(9000 = T \times 15\)\par \(T = \frac{9000}{15} = 600\) [M1]\par Now using \(F = ma\):
Resolving horizontally: \(T=350\) [B1]\par Power = \(Fv\)\par \(9000=350v\)\par \(v=\frac{9000}{350}\)\par \(v=25.71\dots\)\par The maximum speed is \(25.7 \mathrm{~m~s}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 9

A car of mass 1000kg is travelling along a straight horizontal road. The car's engine is working at 12kW. When its speed is \(24 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) its acceleration is \(0.2 \mathrm{m s}^{-2}\). The resistances to motion have a total magnitude of R newtons. Calculate the value of R. [4 marks]
Question 11

A van of mass 1200kg is travelling up a straight road inclined at \(5^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The van moves at a constant speed of \(20 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) and its engine is working at 24kW. The resistance to motion from non-gravitational forces has magnitude R newtons.\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the value of R. [3 marks]\par The road now becomes horizontal. The resistance to motion from non-gravitational forces is unchanged.\par \textbf{b)} Calculate the initial acceleration of the van. [4 marks]

Power \(= Fv\)\par \(24000=T\times 20\)\par \(T=\frac{24000}{20}=1200\) [M1]\par Resolving parallel to the slope:\par \(T=R+1200g\sin 5^{\circ}\)\par \(1200=R+1200g\sin 5^{\circ}\) [M1]\par \(R=1200-1200g\sin 5^{\circ}\)\par \(R=175.04\dots\)\par The value of \(R\) is 175 (3 s.f.) [A1]\par b
\(a\approx 0.8541\dots\)\par The initial acceleration of the van is \(0.854\text{ m s}^{-2}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 12

A car of mass 800kg is travelling at \(18 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) along a straight horizontal road. The car's engine is working at a constant rate of 26kW against a constant resistance of magnitude 750N.\par \textbf{a)} Find the acceleration of the car. [3 marks]\par The car now ascends a straight hill, inclined at \(9^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The resistance to motion from non-gravitational forces is unchanged and the car's engine works at the same rate.\par \textbf{b)} Find the maximum speed at which the car can travel up the hill. [4 marks]

Power \(= Fv\)\par \(26000=T\times 18\)\par \(T=\frac{26000}{18}\) [M1]\par Using \(F=ma:\)\par \(T-750=800a\) [M1]\par \(800a=\frac{26000}{18}-750\)\par \(a=0.8680\dots\)\par The acceleration is \(0.868\mathrm{m s}^{-2}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]\par b\par Resolving parallel to the slope:\par \(T=750+800g\sin 9^{\circ}\) [M1] [A1]
Power \(=Fv\)\par \(26000=T\times v\) [M1]\par \(26000=(750+800\times 9.8\sin 9^{\circ})v\)
\(v=\frac{26000}{(750+800\times 9.8\sin 9^{\circ})}\)\par \(v=13.15\dots\)\par The maximum speed is \(13.2\mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 13

A van of mass 1500 kg is travelling at its maximum speed of \(30 \mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) along a straight horizontal road against a constant resistance of magnitude 600 N.\par \textbf{a)} Find the power developed by the van's engine. [3 marks]\par The van now travels up a hill along a straight road inclined at \(8^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The van's engine works at the same rate and the resistance to motion from non-gravitational forces is unchanged.\par \textbf{b)} Find the maximum speed at which the van can ascend the hill. [4 marks]

Resolving horizontally: \(T=600\) [B1]\par Power \(= Fv\)\par \(= 600\times 30\) [M1]\par \(= 18000\)\par The power is 18 000 W (or 18 kW) [A1]\par b\par Resolving parallel to the slope:\par \(T=600+1500g\sin 8^{\circ}\) [M1] [A1]\par Power \(= Fv\)\par \(18000=(600+1500g\sin 8^{\circ})v\) [M1]
\(v=\frac{18000}{(600+1500g\sin 8^{\circ})}\)\par \(=6.803\dots\)\par The maximum speed is \(6.80\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 15

A train of mass 150 tonnes is moving up a straight track which is inclined at \(2^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. The resistance to the motion of the train from non-gravitational forces has magnitude 6kN and the train's engine is working at a constant rate of 350kW.\par \textbf{a)} Calculate the maximum speed of the train. [5 marks]\par The track now becomes horizontal. The engine continues to work at 350kW and the resistance to motion remains 6kN.\par \textbf{b)} Find the initial acceleration of the train. [3 marks]

Resolving parallel to the slope:\par \(T = (6 \times 10^3) + (150 \times 10^3 g \sin 2^\circ)\) [M1] [A1]\par Power \(= Fv\) [M1]\par \(350 \times 10^3 = (6 \times 10^3 + 150 \times 10^3 g \sin 2^\circ) \times v\) [A1]\par \(v = \frac{350}{(6 + 150 \times 9.8 \sin 2^\circ)} = 6.107 \dots\)\par The maximum speed is \(6.11 \text{ m s}^{-1}\) [A1]\par b\par Power \(= Fv\)
\(350 \times 10^3 = T \times 6.107\)\par \(T = \frac{350 \times 10^3}{6.107}\) [M1]\par Using \(F = ma\):
\(T - 6 \times 10^3 = 150 \times 10^3 \times a\) [M1]

\(\frac{350 \times 10^3}{6.107} - 6 \times 10^3 = 150 \times 10^3 \times a\)\par \(150a = \frac{350}{6.107} - 6\)\par \(a = 0.3420 \dots\)\par The initial acceleration is \(0.342 \text{ m s}^{-2}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 16

A car is moving along a straight horizontal road with speed \(v\mathrm{m s}^{-1}\). The magnitude of the resistance to motion of the car is given by the formula \((150+3 v) \mathrm{N}\). The car's engine is working at 10kW. Calculate the maximum value of \(v\) [6 marks]

Power \(= 10 \mathrm{~kW}=10000 \mathrm{~W}\)\par Power \(= T v\)\par \(10000=T v\)\par \(T=\frac{10000}{v}\) [M1]\par When the velocity is maximum, the acceleration \(= 0 \mathrm{~m s}^{-2}\)\par Therefore the resultant force is \(0 \mathrm{~N}\). Resolving horizontally: [B1]\par \(T=150+3 v\)\par So \(\frac{10000}{v}=150+3 v\) [M1]\par \(10000=150 v+3 v^{2}\)
Rearranging:\par \(3 v^{2}+150 v-10000=0\) [A1]\par Using the quadratic formula:

\(v=\frac{-150 \pm \sqrt{150^{2}-4 \times 3 \times(-10000)}}{6}\) [M1]\par \(v=\frac{-150 \pm \sqrt{142500}}{6}\)\par Since \(v>0\), \(v=\frac{-150+\sqrt{142500}}{6}=37.91\dots\)\par The maximum value of \(v\) is \(37.9 \mathrm{~m s}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
Question 17

A van of mass 4000 kg is travelling in a straight line.\par At the instant when the speed of the car is \(v\mathrm{m s}^{-1}\) the total resistances to motion are modelled as a variable force of magnitude \((1200+8v)\) N. The engine of the van works at a constant rate of 28 kW.\par Problem-solving\par For part b, use P=Fv to find the driving force in terms of w.\par \textbf{a)} Find the acceleration of the van at the instant when \(v=10.\) [4 marks]\par When the car is travelling at \(w\mathrm{m s}^{-1}\), it is decelerating at \(0.2\mathrm{m s}^{-2}.\)\par \textbf{b)} Find the value of w. [4 marks]

Power \(= 28 \text{ kW} = 28000 \text{ W}\)\par Power \(= Tv\)\par \(28000 = Tv\)\par \(T = \frac{28000}{v}\) [M1]\par Resolving horizontally and using \(F = ma\):\par \(\frac{28000}{v} - (1200 + 8v) = 4000a\) [M1]\par When \(v = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}\):\par \(2800 - (1200 + 80) = 4000a\) [A1]\par \(1520 = 4000a\)
So \(a = \frac{1520}{4000} = 0.38 \text{ m s}^{-2}\) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Using \(P = Fv\), when the van is travelling at speed \(w\):

Resistive force \(= 1200 + 8w\)\par As in part a, resolving horizontally and using \(F = ma\):\par \(\frac{28000}{w} - (1200 + 8w) = 4000a\) [M1]\par When \(v = w \text{ m s}^{-1}\), \(a = -0.2 \text{ m s}^{-2}\):\par \(\frac{28000}{w} - (1200 + 8w) = 4000 \times (-0.2)\) [A1]\par \(28000 - 1200w - 8w^2 = -800w\)\par \(8w^2 + 400w - 28000 = 0\)\par \(w^2 + 50w - 3500 = 0\) [M1]\par Using the quadratic formula:\par \(w = \frac{-50 \pm \sqrt{50^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-3500)}}{2} = \frac{-50 \pm \sqrt{16500}}{2}\)\par Since \(w > 0\), \(w = \frac{-50 + \sqrt{16500}}{2} = 39.22\ldots\)
The value of \(w\) is 39.2 (3 s.f.) [A1]
